text: In Husserl's analysis of internal time-consciousness, 'retention' is best characterized as:
choices: A voluntary act of re-presenting (recollecting) a past experience
The immediate presence of the just-past as just-past, not an act of recall
The anticipatory presence of what is immediately about to arrive
The primal impression of the current instant
explanation: Retention is the immediate, non-thematic presence of the just-past AS just-past — I am still experientially present to the note without recalling it. Husserl sharply separates it from recollection (a voluntary re-presenting of a past event), from protention (anticipation of the upcoming), and from the primal impression (the now itself).
